title: Count the Number of Inversions
summary: Given an integer n and a 2D array requirements, where each element in requirements is a pair [endi, cnti] representing the end index and the exact inversion count for that requirement, find the number of permutations of the array [0, 1, 2, ..., n-1] such that for each requirement, the subarray from the start to endi contains exactly cnti inversions.
statement: Given an integer n and a 2D array requirements, where each element in requirements is a pair [endi, cnti] representing the end index and the exact inversion count for that requirement, find the number of permutations of the array [0, 1, 2, ..., n-1] such that for each requirement, the subarray from the start to endi contains exactly cnti inversions. Since the result can be very large, return it modulo 10^9 + 7 .
constraints: n is positive; each requirement [end,count] fixes inversions in permutation positions 0 through end.
Requirement end indices are distinct, and a missing prefix has no inversion restriction.
Count permutations of 0 through n-1 satisfying every requirement, modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: Inserting the new largest value into a length-L permutation adds any inversion count from zero through L-1.
Use inversion-count DP with a sliding window, and zero all states except a required count whenever a constrained prefix is reached.
Every length-L permutation uniquely removes its largest value to one prior permutation plus its insertion contribution, so the recurrence counts each once.

tests.explanation: The permutations [1,2,0] and [2,0,1] each have two total inversions and satisfy the length-one prefix.
Only the fully increasing permutation has zero inversions in both constrained prefixes.
